 ADVERTISEMENT Home lifestyle Post-festive skincare: After the sparkle, comes the glow Tini Sara Anien speaks to experts about tackling post-Deepavali dullness and restoring skin and hair after exposure to smoke, dust and pollution. Tini Sara Anien Last Updated 14 November 2026, 08:30 IST Follow Us Skincare. A simple moisturising routine helps replenish hydration and restore the skin after exposure to smoke, dust and pollutants.
 iStock
The festivities may be over, but their effects can linger on your skin and hair. Exposure to firecracker smoke, dust, pollutants, heavy make-up and styling products can leave skin feeling dull, dry or irritated, while the scalp and hair may accumulate dirt and residue. Instead elaborate treatments or aggressive cleansing, a few simple changes to your daily routine can help. Here are some ways to give yourself a post-Deepavali reset.
 Start with cleansing 
Firecracker smoke, dust and pollutants can settle on the skin, potentially triggering irritation and breakouts. “Wash your face with a mild, pH-balanced cleanser to remove accumulated dirt and impurities. If you have been wearing heavy make-up, use a gentle cleansing balm or micellar water before washing your face,” says dermatologist Dr Akansha M. Avoid harsh scrubs and excessive washing, as these can strip the skin of its natural oils.
She adds that smoke, dust and styling products can accumulate on the scalp, leaving it itchy or uncomfortable. “Wash your hair with a mild shampoo, concentrating on cleansing the scalp rather than aggressively scrubbing the lengths. Those with oily scalps may need more frequent washing, while people with dry scalps should avoid overwashing,” she explains. If residue persists, a second gentle wash may help.
 Follow a routine 
Different skin types respond differently to environmental exposure. “People with oily skin can opt for a gentle gel-based cleanser and a lightweight, non-comedogenic moisturiser to prevent clogged pores. Dry skin benefits from cream-based cleansers and richer moisturisers containing ceramides, glycerin or hyaluronic acid,” explains Dr Deepika H, another dermatologist. If you have combination skin, use a balanced approach: lightweight hydration for the oily T-zone (forehead, nose and chin) and a slightly richer moisturiser on drier areas such as the cheeks.
 Restore the skin barrier 
Frequent cleansing, pollution exposure and weather changes can leave the skin barrier compromised. Look for moisturisers containing ceramides, panthenol or hyaluronic acid to replenish hydration and soothe the skin. Avoid introducing multiple active ingredients, such as exfoliating acids and retinol, immediately after experiencing irritation, says Dr Deepika. Give your skin time to recover before resuming an intensive skincare routine.
 Don’t skip sunscreen 
Even after the festivities, protecting your skin from UV exposure remains essential. Apply a sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every morning. Choose a lightweight, gel-based formula if you have oily skin, or a moisturising cream-based sunscreen if your skin is dry. Reapply every two hours when outdoors.
 Nourish tresses 
Hair exposed to pollution and frequent styling may feel dry, rough and tangled. Use a conditioner after shampooing, where you concentrate on the mid-lengths and ends. “A hydrating hair mask once a week can help improve softness and manageability. Those with oily hair should opt for lightweight formulations, while dry or chemically treated hair may benefit from richer conditioning products,” says Dr Akansha. Avoid excessive heat styling while your hair recovers.
 Take a breather 
Give your skin a break from heavy make-up and your hair a pause from elaborate styling for a few days. Dr Akansha asserts that prioritising adequate sleep, hydration and a balanced diet is important. “Include foods rich in antioxidants, vitamins and healthy fats to support overall skin and hair health,” she adds.
